findings.category: A01: Broken Access Control / A04: Insecure Design
findings.title: users.id (and every FK'd user_id column) uses a case- and accent-insensitive collation — verified live to collide across genuinely distinct identity strings, with blast radius broader than previously assessed
findings.description:
Live testing against poshivon_test (MariaDB 11.4, schema from migration 004) confirms `users.id` inherits `utf8mb4_uca1400_ai_ci` from the database default, and — critically — so do `user_settings.user_id`, `chats.user_id`, `calculations.user_id`, and `access_requests.user_id` (none of these columns carry an explicit COLLATE override; verified via SHOW CREATE TABLE on all five tables). This is a case-insensitive, accent-insensitive, trailing-space-insensitive (PAD SPACE) collation.

Live reproduction: running the exact upsert shape used by `EnsureUser` (postgres.go:615-635) with login `'rogogdbd'` against a database that already has the seeded admin row `'RoGogDBD'` does NOT create a second row — it matches the PRIMARY KEY of the existing admin row and updates that row's `email`/`display_name` to attacker-supplied values, while `role`/`has_access` (correctly, per Decision 11) are left untouched. Further live checks: `'RoGogDBD' = 'ROGOGDBD'` under this collation → true; `'RoGogDBD' = 'RoGogDBD '` (trailing space) → true; cross-script Cyrillic homoglyph (`'irina2000аleshina'` with Cyrillic а U+0430) → false (cross-script does NOT collide, so homoglyph spoofing via a different script is not viable here).

Why this is broader than the risk already carried forward from Task 1: Task 1's decisions.md frames this purely as 'benign... verified live: rogogdbd collides with the seeded row instead of creating a second admin' — i.e. it only checked that a duplicate admin row isn't created. It did not check (a) that the SAME collation applies to every table this task's EnsureUser/GetUser/SetAccess touch (user_settings, chats, calculations, access_requests all inherit it too, since none of them carry an explicit COLLATE), and (b) the actual consequence of the collision: `GetUser('rogogdbd')` returns the seeded admin's row (role=admin, has_access=true) via the exact same collation-driven match — this is not just 'no duplicate row', it is 'a different login string resolves to the admin's identity and every table keyed by that identity'. If any Yandex account exists (or can be created) whose login differs from `RoGogDBD` or `irina2000aleshina` only by case, a trailing space, or a diacritic, that account's session would, through `EnsureUser`/`GetUser` as implemented in this task, read and write the seeded admin's row — inheriting `role='admin'`, `has_access=true`, and access to that identity's chats/settings/calculations. The same collation collapse also merges any two ordinary (non-admin) users whose logins fold to the same value, causing one account's `user_settings`/`chats`/`calculations` rows to become shared/overwritten by the other.

The repository layer performs no exact-match verification anywhere — `Where("id = ?", login)` (postgres.go:641, 673-675, 684, 730, 752-754) and the raw `access_requests` upsert (postgres.go:709-724) all rely solely on the column's ambient collation for equality. `service.requireLogin` (access.go:223-230) only checks for emptiness and a rune-count bound; there is no case/whitespace/normalization step anywhere in the login path (grep confirms no `ToLower`/`TrimSpace`/normalization on the login value in access.go or postgres.go).

Whether this is exploitable in practice depends on an assumption this codebase does not control or verify: that Yandex's own username system never allows two distinct accounts to register logins that fold to the same value under `utf8mb4_uca1400_ai_ci` (case, primary-weight accent, and trailing whitespace). That is an external, unverified precondition being used as a de facto access-control boundary — exactly the kind of implicit trust in an unverified third-party invariant that A04 (Insecure Design) flags. Task 1's decisions.md records this as 'raised... deliberately not patched' but, unlike the separate public-repo-exposure finding in the same file, it does not record an explicit user decision to accept the risk — it was deferred without a recorded decision.
findings.impact: If a Yandex account with a login that case/accent/whitespace-folds to `RoGogDBD` or `irina2000aleshina` exists or can be created, that account inherits the admin role and access flag on next login — full administrative privilege escalation (view/grant/revoke access for all users) without ever going through the approval flow the whole feature exists to enforce (violates US-6, US-13, US-14). For non-admin accounts, two genuinely distinct people whose logins fold together would silently share one `users` row and all data hanging off it (settings, chats, calculations, access requests) — cross-account data disclosure and corruption.
findings.recommendation: This cannot be fully fixed inside Task 3's repository code alone — the root cause is the column collation set by Task 1's migration (out of this task's scope to alter) and the tech-spec's choice to key identity by the mutable Yandex `login` string rather than Yandex's immutable numeric account id. Recommend re-opening this as an explicit tech-spec decision before shipping, with one of: (a) change `users.id` and the four dependent `user_id` columns to an explicit case-sensitive, non-PAD-SPACE collation (e.g. `utf8mb4_bin` or `utf8mb4_0900_as_cs` if available on this MariaDB version) in a follow-up migration, re-validating the two seeded admin rows still match exactly; or (b) key identity by Yandex's numeric `id` instead of `login`, storing `login` only as a display field. As a stop-gap defense-in-depth inside this task's queries, `EnsureUser`/`GetUser`/`SetAccess` could additionally verify `login == record.ID` (byte-exact) after a collation-matched read and treat a mismatch as `ErrNotFound` rather than silently operating on the folded row — this narrows the blast radius without requiring a schema change, though it does not fix the underlying PRIMARY KEY collision (MariaDB will still refuse to INSERT a second row for a folding-equal login; verified live that the very first write for a colliding login lands on the existing row, so the mismatch would need to be caught at EnsureUser time, not just at read time).
findings.cwe: CWE-178: Improper Handling of Case Sensitivity

findings.title: SetAccess and DecideRequest remain two independent, non-transactional repository calls — the Task 2 snapshot race is unaddressed by Task 3's implementation
findings.description:
Task 2's decisions.md explicitly forwarded this to Task 3: 'the real fix is one transaction in the repository, which is Task 3's layer.' Reviewing the actual implementation, `SetAccess` (postgres.go:671-691, memory.go:275-288) and `DecideRequest` (postgres.go:751-764, memory.go:323-338) remain fully independent operations against different tables/maps with no shared transaction — the service layer (`AccessService.SetAccess`, outside this task) calls them as two sequential, non-atomic steps. Additionally, `PostgresRepository.SetAccess` itself performs two round trips (an `UPDATE` followed by a `SELECT COUNT` on the zero-rows-affected branch, postgres.go:672-690) that are not wrapped together either, so a concurrent delete/insert of the same login between the two calls could misclassify the outcome (low-impact: this path is only reachable by an authenticated admin per the intended authz model, and misclassification only affects error-code accuracy, not the access flag itself).

The concrete consequence, per Task 2's own analysis: a `CreateRequest` that lands between the `SetAccess` UPDATE and the `DecideRequest` UPDATE either (a) stays `pending` forever and is invisible to future decisions once access has already been granted (the next `CreateRequest` short-circuits on `ErrConflict`), or (b) gets stamped `approved`/`rejected` with an admin's `decided_by` though nobody actually reviewed that specific submission. `has_access` itself is never wrong — this affects only the `access_requests` audit trail (Decision 5's `decided_by`/`decided_at` provenance), which is a logging/monitoring integrity concern (A09) more than an access-control bypass.
findings.impact: Under concurrent admin-decision and user-request-submission traffic, the access_requests table can end up with a stale pending row that never gets revisited, or a decision falsely attributed to an admin who didn't review that particular submission — an audit-trail integrity gap, not a privilege-escalation path (verified: has_access is written with exactly the value the admin requested in every code path read).
findings.recommendation: If this is meant to be fully closed in this task, wrap the two writes in a single DB transaction in `PostgresRepository` (the interfaces as specified by Task 2 don't expose a combined method, so either add one, or have the service layer receive a repository-level transactional helper). If it is intentionally deferred to a later task, record that explicitly in this task's decisions.md entry rather than leaving it implicit — Task 2's note already flagged it as 'Task 3's layer' and this task's summary should state whether it was picked up or knowingly deferred again.
findings.cwe: CWE-362: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition')

findings.title: Test-fixture DSN documented with plaintext dev credentials in a comment
findings.description: access_repo_test.go:23-25 documents an example `TEST_DB_DSN` value containing the literal credential pair `poshivon:poshivon`. This matches the project's known local/dev-only database credential (consistent with the docker-compose local setup and the DSN the orchestrator itself supplied for this review), not a production secret, and it appears only in a doc comment as an example, not as a hardcoded value actually used by the code (the code reads it from the environment via `os.Getenv(testDBDSNEnv)`, postgres.go/access_repo_test.go:58).
findings.impact: None in practice — this is a well-known local-only credential pair, not exploitable against any real environment, and is not compiled into any binary or committed as an active default.
findings.recommendation: No action required; noting for completeness per the mandatory hardcoded-secrets scan. If desired, the example could use an obviously-fake placeholder (e.g. `user:pass@tcp(...)`) instead of the real local dev credential to avoid any future confusion, but this is cosmetic.

verification_performed: Read postgres.go, memory.go, and access_repo_test.go in full (not as a diff).
Read user-spec.md, tech-spec.md (both pages), decisions.md (Task 1 and Task 2 entries), and tasks/3.md in full.
Confirmed poshivon_db container running (mariadb:11.4) with migrations 001-004 already applied to poshivon_test.

Live-verified Decision 13: userModel (postgres.go:25-28) has only ID and CreatedAt fields, carries the required invariant comment; a separate userAccessModel/userAccessRow handle role/has_access/email/display_name.
Live-ran `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `gofmt -l` on the three task files via golang:1.25-alpine — all clean.

Live-ran the full access_repo_test.go contract suite with TEST_DB_DSN set — all TestAccessRepoContract_* tests passed against both MemoryRepository and PostgresRepository, including TestAccessRepoContract_EnsureUserPreservesAdminRoleAndAccess (Decision 11 regression), TestAccessRepoContract_CreateRequestRowsAffectedSemantics (Decision 5's 1/0/2 RowsAffected contract, confirmed live against the real driver), and TestAccessRepoContract_ExistingWritePathsSurviveAccessColumns (Decision 13 regression against the live chk_users_role CHECK constraint).

Live-probed the collation behavior directly against the DB (see major finding above): case-fold collision, trailing-space collision, cross-script Cyrillic homoglyph non-collision, and confirmed the same collation is inherited by user_settings/chats/calculations/access_requests via SHOW CREATE TABLE on all five tables.
Restored the test database to its pre-audit state (removed probe rows, reset the seeded RoGogDBD row's email/display_name to NULL) after live testing.

Read through every SQL statement and GORM call in postgres.go and access_repo_test.go for injection surface: every query uses parameter placeholders (`?`) or GORM's clause builders; no string concatenation of caller-controlled input into SQL was found anywhere in this task's files.

Reviewed the touchUserRow helper (memory.go:340-354) added to MemoryRepository's UpsertSettings/CreateChat/AppendCalculation: it explicitly sets Role=service.RoleUser and HasAccess=false (never leaves them as Go zero-values that could be misread), mirroring Postgres's existing upsertUser (postgres.go:796-801) exactly — no new privilege data is exposed and no new authorization exposure is introduced beyond what already exists in the unauthenticated legacy /api/v1/users/* surface (unchanged, pre-existing, and explicitly still Task 6's responsibility to close).

Checked go.mod: no new dependencies added by this task (tech-spec confirms 'Новых модулей не добавляется'); existing versions (gorm v1.31.0, go-sql-driver/mysql v1.8.1, prometheus/client_golang v1.22.0) are recent and were not modified here.
